name: Noah and the ark: the raven, the dove, and the olive leaf
scope: T1: Noah builds a huge wooden ark on dry land at God's warning while the neighbors mock him; his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth help. T2: pairs of every animal walk aboard, the rain falls for forty days and forty nights, and the fountains of the deep burst open (Genesis 7:11); the ark floats while the mountains vanish under water. T3: after the waters begin to fall, Noah opens a window and sends out a RAVEN, which flies to and fro until the waters dry up (Genesis 8:7). T4: then he sends out a DOVE three times — first she finds no rest for her foot and returns; the second time she comes back at evening with a freshly plucked OLIVE LEAF in her beak (Genesis 8:11); the third time she does not return. T5: the ark comes to rest on the mountains of ARARAT (Genesis 8:4); Noah builds an altar, and God sets his BOW in the cloud as a sign of the covenant that he will never again flood the earth (Genesis 9:13). Further rungs: the raven vs. dove contrast (unclean scavenger sent first, clean bird sent second); Methuselah as Noah's grandfather living 969 years and dying in the year of the flood by rabbinic tradition; the three sons and the shame of Ham after Noah plants a vineyard (Genesis 9:20-25); the covenant sign that God will not use water again.
source: Grokipedia 'Noah' + 'Noah's Ark' (read via browser if 403); Genesis 6-9 KJV; Wikipedia 'Noah's Ark' for cultural-reception notes only; primary: Genesis 7:11, 8:4, 8:7, 8:11, 9:13.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: the OLIVE LEAF at T4 — parents remember the dove but not that Noah sent the raven FIRST or that the leaf was olive. DISTRACTOR MINE at T3/T4: swap in the wrong bird (eagle / sparrow / owl) and the wrong plant (fig leaf / palm frond / vine); at T5 swap Ararat for Sinai / Moriah / Nebo. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T4 stem sets the scene — 'On the second flight the bird returned at evening carrying a freshly plucked leaf. What kind of leaf?' — never names 'olive' before the choices. SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the same way you'd tell Deucalion's Greek flood or Utnapishtim's Babylonian one — plain narrative 'Noah', not 'the righteous man of God'. No 'the Lord' — 'God' as story-agent is fine, same as 'Zeus' in a Greek ladder.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns Mount Ararat as a real place in eastern Turkey (elevation, volcano); theology owns the ark landing there in story. No history overlap.

name: Abraham called from Ur to Canaan and the covenant of stars
scope: T1: an old man named Abram leaves his home in UR of the Chaldeans with his wife Sarai and his nephew Lot, told by God to go to a land he has never seen (Genesis 12:1). T2: he arrives in CANAAN and builds altars at Shechem and between Bethel and Ai; God promises the land to his descendants though he has no children. T3: God takes Abram outside at night and says 'Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them ... so shall thy seed be' (Genesis 15:5). T4: God changes his name from ABRAM to ABRAHAM ('father of many nations') and Sarai to SARAH; the covenant sign is CIRCUMCISION (Genesis 17:5, 17:10). T5: three MYSTERIOUS VISITORS come to Abraham's tent at the oaks of MAMRE; he runs to fetch a calf and cakes; they tell Sarah, listening from the tent door, that she will bear a son within a year, and she LAUGHS (Genesis 18:12) — so the son is named ISAAC ('he laughs'). Further rungs: Lot's separation and the choice of Sodom's plain; Melchizedek the priest-king of Salem bringing bread and wine and blessing Abram (Genesis 14:18); Hagar the Egyptian maid bearing Ishmael; the destruction of Sodom and Lot's wife looking back and becoming a pillar of salt.
source: Grokipedia 'Abraham' (browser); Genesis 12, 15, 17, 18 KJV; Wikipedia 'Abraham' for Ur-location context; primary: Genesis 12:1, 15:5, 17:5, 18:12.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: SARAH LAUGHING at the tent door — parents know Abraham, few remember the laugh becomes the name Isaac. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T1 swap Ur for Haran / Babylon / Nineveh; at T4 swap circumcision for baptism / sacrifice / anointing; at T5 swap Sarah for Hagar / Rebekah / Rachel. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T3 stem 'God took him outside at night and told him to count something impossible — what did he point to?' — never names 'stars' first. SYMMETRIC-VOICE: same voice as telling of Odysseus called by Athena, no 'the Lord promised' — 'God promised' as story-agent parallel to 'Zeus promised'.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns Ur as an archaeological Sumerian city; theology owns the call OUT of Ur. HISTORY owns Bronze Age Mesopotamia; theology owns the covenant story.

name: Hagar and Ishmael sent into the wilderness and the well
scope: T1: Sarah has waited years for a child and cannot bear one, so she gives her Egyptian maid HAGAR to Abraham; Hagar bears a son named ISHMAEL (Genesis 16:15). T2: after Isaac is born and weaned, Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and demands Abraham cast out the maid and her son; Abraham gives Hagar bread and a bottle of water and sends her into the wilderness of BEERSHEBA (Genesis 21:14). T3: the water in the bottle is spent; Hagar lays the boy under a shrub and sits a bowshot away, saying 'Let me not see the death of the child' (Genesis 21:16), and she lifts up her voice and weeps. T4: an angel of God calls to her out of heaven and says 'What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not' (Genesis 21:17); then God opens her eyes and she sees a WELL of water and fills the bottle. T5: earlier, when she first fled Sarah's harshness, Hagar had already met the angel by a fountain in the way to Shur and named that spring BEER-LAHAI-ROI — 'the well of the Living One who sees me' (Genesis 16:14) — the only person in Genesis to give God a name. Further rungs: Ishmael becomes an archer in the wilderness of Paran; his twelve sons become princes; the promise that his hand will be against every man; the covenant that he too becomes a great nation.
source: Grokipedia 'Hagar' (browser); Genesis 16, 21 KJV; primary: Genesis 16:14, 21:14-19; Wikipedia 'Hagar' for the Beer-lahai-roi etymology.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T5 — Hagar is the only person in Genesis who NAMES God. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T2 swap Beersheba for Sinai / Moab / Paran; at T4 swap 'a well' for 'a raven brought bread' / 'a stream from a rock' (both real other-Bible miracles); at T5 swap the well's name for real other place-names (Massah / Meribah / Bethel). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T4 stem — 'The water was gone and she wept. Then God opened her eyes to see WHAT?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the sober narrative you'd use for a Greek mother-in-exile — no 'God provided' triumphalism. Hagar's dignity and grief carried straight.
history_overlap: None direct. Ishmael-as-ancestor is claimed by later Arab tradition; theology bank stays with the STORY, not the ethnic-descent debate.

name: The binding of Isaac on Mount Moriah
scope: T1: God tests Abraham by telling him to take his son ISAAC — his only son, whom he loves — to a mountain God will show him, and offer him as a burnt offering (Genesis 22:2). T2: Abraham saddles his ass early in the morning, cleaves the wood for the offering, and takes two young men and Isaac; on the third day he sees the place afar off. T3: Isaac carries the wood on his back up the mountain; he asks his father, 'Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the LAMB for a burnt offering?' — and Abraham answers, 'My son, God will provide himself a lamb' (Genesis 22:7-8). T4: at the top Abraham builds an altar, binds Isaac, lays him on the wood, and stretches out his hand with the KNIFE — and an angel of the Lord calls from heaven, 'Lay not thine hand upon the lad' (Genesis 22:12). T5: Abraham looks and behind him a RAM is caught in a THICKET by its horns; he takes the ram and offers it in place of his son, and calls the place JEHOVAH-JIREH ('the Lord will provide', Genesis 22:14); the mountain is MORIAH, later identified by tradition with the Temple Mount in Jerusalem. Further rungs: the three-day journey; the two servants left at the foot; Isaac's silence in most tellings; the promise renewed that his seed will be as the stars.
source: Grokipedia 'Binding of Isaac' (browser); Genesis 22 KJV; primary: Genesis 22:2, 22:7-8, 22:12, 22:14; the Aqedah in Jewish tradition (Wikipedia 'Binding of Isaac').
framing_note: DINNER TEST: the RAM in the THICKET at T5 — everyone remembers the knife stopped, few remember what replaced Isaac. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T5 swap the ram for a lamb / a goat / a bullock (all real biblical offerings); at T2/T5 swap Moriah for Sinai / Horeb / Nebo / Ararat; at T3 swap 'lamb' for 'bullock' / 'dove' (all real offerings). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T5 stem 'Abraham lifted his eyes and saw an animal caught by its HORNS in a thicket. What animal?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the same dread you'd bring to Agamemnon and Iphigeneia at Aulis — the parallel is a real point of comparative myth. No 'God tested his faithful servant' triumphal frame; the story's horror is left in.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns the Temple Mount as a place; theology owns Moriah as the story-mountain of the binding.

name: Jacob's ladder at Bethel and the wrestling angel at Peniel
scope: T1: JACOB flees his brother Esau, whose birthright he bought with lentil stew and whose blessing he stole by wearing goatskins on his arms so his blind father Isaac would feel hair (Genesis 27). T2: on the road at a certain place he takes a stone for his pillow and sleeps; he dreams of a LADDER set on the earth whose top reaches to heaven, and the angels of God ascending and descending on it (Genesis 28:12). T3: he wakes and says, 'Surely the Lord is in this place; and I knew it not' (Genesis 28:16); he sets up the pillow-stone as a pillar, pours oil on it, and calls the place BETHEL — 'the house of God'. T4: years later, returning home, he sends his family and flocks across the ford of the brook JABBOK, and is left alone; a MAN wrestles with him until the breaking of the day (Genesis 32:24) and touches the hollow of his THIGH so that it is out of joint. T5: Jacob will not let him go until he blesses him; the stranger says, 'Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but ISRAEL: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed' (Genesis 32:28); Jacob calls the place PENIEL — 'I have seen God face to face' — and goes on limping. Further rungs: Esau running to meet him and falling on his neck; Rachel at the well and Laban's twenty years; the striped and speckled sheep; the twelve sons who become the tribes; Rachel dying in childbirth naming Benjamin.
source: Grokipedia 'Jacob' + 'Jacob's Ladder' (browser); Genesis 25, 27, 28, 32 KJV; primary: Genesis 28:12, 28:16, 32:24, 32:28.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: the touched HIP-JOINT / limp at T4 — most people remember the wrestling, few remember he limps the rest of his life. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T2 swap 'ladder' for 'chariot' / 'staircase of fire' (Elijah's chariot is real); at T4/T5 swap Peniel for Bethel / Jabbok / Mahanaim (all real story-places); at T5 swap Israel for Isaac / Ishmael / Immanuel. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T5 stem — 'The stranger touched his hip out of joint and would not tell his name, but gave Jacob a new one meaning "one who has struggled with God". What was it?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Heracles wrestling the river-god Achelous — a mortal grappling a numen and being marked by it. Named for what happened, not doctrine.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns Bethel and the Jabbok as real places in the Levant; theology owns the ladder-dream and the wrestling.

name: Joseph's coat of many colors and the pit at Dothan
scope: T1: JOSEPH is the favorite son of Jacob, born to Rachel in his old age; Jacob makes him a COAT OF MANY COLORS (Genesis 37:3) and his ten older brothers hate him for it. T2: Joseph dreams that his sheaf stands upright and the eleven other sheaves bow to it; he dreams the sun and moon and eleven stars bow to him; the brothers say, 'Behold, this DREAMER cometh' (Genesis 37:19). T3: at DOTHAN they strip off the coat, throw him into a PIT with no water in it, and sit down to eat bread; a caravan of Ishmaelites comes by carrying spices to Egypt and they sell him for TWENTY PIECES OF SILVER (Genesis 37:28). T4: they dip the coat in the blood of a slain kid and bring it to Jacob, saying, 'Know now whether it be thy son's coat or no'; Jacob tears his clothes and mourns for many days (Genesis 37:32-34). T5: in Egypt Joseph is bought by Potiphar, thrown into prison after Potiphar's wife lies about him grabbing her garment, and there he interprets the dreams of the BUTLER and the BAKER — the butler restored, the baker hanged (Genesis 40) — which is how Pharaoh will hear of him. Further rungs: Reuben trying to save him and returning to find him gone; Judah proposing the sale; the caravan carrying balm, spicery, and myrrh; Joseph's shirt-of-blood becoming the first false evidence in Scripture.
source: Grokipedia 'Joseph (Genesis)' (browser); Genesis 37, 39, 40 KJV; primary: Genesis 37:3, 37:19, 37:28, 40; Wikipedia 'Joseph's coat' for the ketonet passim translation debate.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: TWENTY pieces of silver — everyone remembers Judas's thirty, few remember Joseph's twenty. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T3 swap the price (thirty / ten / fifteen — thirty is the Judas trap); swap Dothan for Shechem / Beersheba / Hebron; at T5 swap butler+baker for cupbearer+chief steward mislabels. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T3 stem — 'A caravan of Ishmaelites carrying spices to Egypt came by, and the brothers sold Joseph for how much silver?' The pit / caravan detail is scene, the number is the ask. SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Bellerophon being framed by Anteia — a young man wronged by an accuser he refused. Named things: Potiphar's wife, the garment left in her hand, Dothan.
history_overlap: None direct — Joseph as vizier is legendary-historical; the STORY belongs to theology.

name: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams: the seven fat and lean cows
scope: T1: PHARAOH dreams that seven fat cows come up out of the RIVER NILE and feed in a meadow; then seven lean and ill-favored cows come up and eat them, and Pharaoh wakes (Genesis 41:1-4). T2: he dreams a second dream — seven full ears of corn on one stalk, and seven thin ears blasted with the east wind that devour the seven full ears; his magicians cannot interpret it. T3: the chief butler remembers a Hebrew in prison who read his dream true; Joseph is brought hastily out of the DUNGEON, shaves himself, changes his clothes, and stands before Pharaoh. T4: Joseph says the two dreams are ONE — seven years of great plenty followed by seven years of FAMINE so grievous the plenty will be forgotten (Genesis 41:29-30); he advises Pharaoh to appoint a wise man to gather the fifth part of the harvest and store it in cities. T5: Pharaoh takes his SIGNET RING off his hand and puts it on Joseph's hand, dresses him in fine linen and a GOLD CHAIN, and gives him the name ZAPHNATH-PAANEAH (Genesis 41:42-45); he rides in the second chariot and men cry 'Bow the knee' before him. Further rungs: Joseph naming his sons Manasseh ('God has made me forget') and Ephraim ('God has made me fruitful'); the seven years of plenty passing like a blur; the famine reaching Canaan and the brothers coming down to buy grain; the silver cup planted in Benjamin's sack.
source: Grokipedia 'Joseph (Genesis)' — Pharaoh's dreams section (browser); Genesis 41 KJV; primary: Genesis 41:1-4, 41:29-30, 41:42-45.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T5 — Pharaoh's SIGNET RING slipped onto Joseph's hand. Every kid remembers 'fat cows and lean cows', few remember the ring transfer. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T1 swap 'cows' for 'sheep' / 'horses' / 'crocodiles' (Egyptian associations); at T4 swap 'seven years' for 'seven months' / 'seven days'; at T5 swap 'signet ring' for 'crown' / 'staff' / 'crook and flail'. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T5 stem — 'Pharaoh took something off his own hand and put it on Joseph's — what?' The clothing and chariot are scene. SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Daniel reading the wall for Belshazzar, or Melampus reading Iphiclus's condition — dream-reader vindicated. No 'the Lord gave him the gift'; 'Joseph read the dream true' as agent voice.
history_overlap: HISTORY owns the actual Egyptian dynasties; theology owns the vizier-Joseph story, which sits outside firm dynastic identification on purpose.

name: Joseph reveals himself: 'I am Joseph your brother'
scope: T1: the ten brothers come down to Egypt to buy grain and do not know that the vizier they bow to is JOSEPH; he knows them but speaks roughly, accusing them of being spies (Genesis 42:7-9). T2: he demands they bring the youngest brother BENJAMIN — Rachel's other son, whom Jacob will not let go — and holds SIMEON in prison as hostage; the brothers murmur to each other, not knowing Joseph understands their Hebrew, 'We are verily guilty concerning our brother' (Genesis 42:21). T3: on the second trip Joseph feasts them and seats them by AGE in the exact order of birth, and they marvel; he gives Benjamin five times as much food as the others (Genesis 43:33-34). T4: as they leave, Joseph has his silver CUP hidden in Benjamin's sack; his steward overtakes them and finds it, and Judah steps forward and offers to be a slave in Benjamin's place, telling Joseph the tale of an old father whose life is bound up in the boy's life (Genesis 44). T5: Joseph can hold in no longer; he sends every Egyptian out and cries with a loud voice, 'I am JOSEPH; doth my father yet live?' (Genesis 45:3); he says, 'Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good' (Genesis 50:20); he falls on Benjamin's neck and weeps, and kisses all his brothers. Further rungs: Jacob's wagons coming down to Goshen; the seventy souls of the house of Israel; Jacob before Pharaoh saying his days are few and evil; the blessing over the twelve sons on his deathbed.
source: Grokipedia 'Joseph (Genesis)' (browser); Genesis 42-45, 50 KJV; primary: Genesis 42:21, 43:33-34, 45:3, 50:20.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T3 — SEATED BY AGE without a word said. Parents remember the tears and the silver cup but not the seating trick. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T4 swap 'silver cup' for 'gold cup' / 'jeweled ring' / 'signet' (his own signet from prior ladder); at T5 swap the quote for 'am I my brother's keeper?' (Cain, real) / 'let my people go' (Moses, real). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T3 stem — 'Joseph seated the eleven brothers at his feast in an order that astonished them. What order?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Odysseus revealing himself to Telemachus in the swineherd's hut — long-parted kin, the moment of recognition. 'Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good' as story-quote, not doctrine.
history_overlap: None direct.

name: Moses in the basket of bulrushes
scope: T1: a new Pharaoh who does not know Joseph enslaves the Hebrews and orders every male child born to them thrown into the RIVER NILE (Exodus 1:22). T2: a Levite woman (JOCHEBED by later tradition) hides her son three months; when she can hide him no longer she takes an ARK of BULRUSHES, daubs it with slime and pitch, and lays him in it among the flags by the river's brink (Exodus 2:3). T3: his sister MIRIAM stands afar off to watch what will be done to him; PHARAOH'S DAUGHTER comes down to bathe and sees the ark among the flags and sends her maid to fetch it; when she opens it the babe weeps, and she has compassion on him (Exodus 2:5-6). T4: Miriam steps forward and asks if she should fetch a Hebrew nurse for the child; she runs and fetches the boy's own mother, who is paid wages to nurse her own son (Exodus 2:7-9). T5: Pharaoh's daughter names him MOSES 'because I drew him out of the water' (Exodus 2:10); he grows up in Pharaoh's house as a prince of Egypt. Further rungs: Moses as a grown man seeing an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew and killing him and hiding him in the sand; fleeing to Midian and drawing water for the daughters of Jethro at the well; marrying Zipporah; the sons Gershom ('I have been a stranger in a strange land') and Eliezer.
source: Grokipedia 'Moses' (browser); Exodus 1-2 KJV; primary: Exodus 1:22, 2:3, 2:5-10; Josephus Antiquities 2 for the Miriam-vigil detail.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T4 — the birth-mother HIRED as the nurse, paid to nurse her own baby. That reversal shocks. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T2 swap bulrushes for reeds / papyrus stalks / palm leaves (papyrus is close enough to be a serious trap); at T3 swap Miriam for Aaron (real brother) / Zipporah (later wife); at T5 swap the etymology 'drawn out' for wrong Hebrew etymologies. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T4 stem — 'The princess asked for a Hebrew nurse for the crying baby, and Miriam ran and fetched the ONE PERSON in all Egypt who most wanted the job. Who?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Perseus set adrift in the chest with Danae, or Karna floated down the Ganges — the abandoned-infant-rescued type-scene named honestly.
history_overlap: HISTORY owns the debate over Pharaoh identity (Ramesses II vs. Thutmose); theology owns the basket story.

name: The burning bush and the name I AM
scope: T1: MOSES, now a shepherd in Midian, leads the flock of his father-in-law JETHRO to the backside of the desert and comes to HOREB, the mountain of God (Exodus 3:1). T2: an angel appears in a FLAME OF FIRE out of the midst of a BUSH; the bush burns but is not consumed; Moses turns aside to see this great sight (Exodus 3:2-3). T3: God calls out of the bush, 'Moses, Moses ... put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is HOLY GROUND' (Exodus 3:5); Moses hides his face, afraid to look. T4: God tells him to go to Pharaoh and bring the Hebrews out of Egypt; Moses asks, 'Who am I?' and 'When they ask me thy name, what shall I say?' God answers, 'I AM THAT I AM ... Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you' (Exodus 3:14). T5: God gives Moses two signs: his ROD becomes a SERPENT when cast on the ground and a rod again when he takes it by the tail; his hand put in his bosom comes out LEPROUS as snow and clean again when returned. Moses pleads that he is SLOW OF SPEECH — 'not eloquent ... slow of speech, and of a slow tongue' (Exodus 4:10) — so God appoints his brother AARON as his spokesman. Further rungs: Zipporah at the inn cutting off her son's foreskin and casting it at Moses's feet ('a bloody husband art thou to me'); Moses returning to Egypt with rod in hand; Aaron meeting him at the mount of God.
source: Grokipedia 'Burning bush' (browser); Exodus 3-4 KJV; primary: Exodus 3:1-14, 4:10.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T5 — Moses is SLOW OF SPEECH. Everyone remembers the burning bush, few remember Moses's stutter and that Aaron speaks for him. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T1 swap Horeb for Sinai (same mountain but different name — TRAP that's arguably correct; use 'the mountain he later called Horeb' to disambiguate); at T4 swap 'I AM THAT I AM' for 'the Alpha and the Omega' (real, but Revelation) / 'the Ancient of Days' (Daniel). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T3 stem — 'God tells Moses to remove something before approaching. What?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Odin at Mimir's well trading an eye for wisdom — an encounter with a numen at a wild place, marked with a demand. Plain 'God' not 'the Lord'; the tetragrammaton (YHWH) as name-story, not doctrine.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns Sinai/Horeb as a place; theology owns the bush-encounter there.

name: The ten plagues of Egypt
scope: T1: Moses and Aaron go before Pharaoh and say, 'Let my people go' (Exodus 5:1); Pharaoh answers, 'Who is the Lord, that I should obey his voice?' and makes the Hebrews' work harder — they must gather their own STRAW to make bricks. T2: the ten plagues fall in order: (1) the RIVER NILE turned to BLOOD; (2) FROGS in the houses and the kneading troughs; (3) LICE from the dust; (4) FLIES; (5) MURRAIN on the cattle. T3: (6) BOILS breaking forth with blains on man and beast, so Pharaoh's magicians cannot stand before Moses; (7) HAIL mingled with FIRE running along the ground; (8) LOCUSTS carried by the east wind, covering the face of the earth; (9) DARKNESS that may be felt for three days. T4: the tenth plague: the DEATH OF THE FIRSTBORN at midnight, from Pharaoh's firstborn on the throne to the firstborn of the maidservant behind the mill; the Hebrews are told to kill a LAMB at twilight and strike its blood on the LINTEL and two side POSTS of the door with a bunch of HYSSOP (Exodus 12:22), so the destroyer will PASS OVER their houses. T5: the Hebrews eat the lamb roast with fire, with UNLEAVENED BREAD and BITTER HERBS, loins girded, shoes on feet, staff in hand; in the night Pharaoh rises and cries, 'Rise up, and get you forth ... take your flocks and your herds' (Exodus 12:31); the people leave with the Egyptians' GOLD and JEWELRY they have asked for, and no time even to leaven their bread — so they carry dough on their shoulders. Further rungs: the magicians Jannes and Jambres (2 Timothy 3:8) matching the first three plagues then failing; the distinction of Goshen where the plagues do not fall; the memorial of Passover eaten in haste every year after.
source: Grokipedia 'Plagues of Egypt' + 'Passover' (browser); Exodus 5, 7-12 KJV; primary: Exodus 5:1, 12:22, 12:31.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T4 — HYSSOP as the paintbrush for lamb's blood on the doorposts. Everyone knows the plagues; few remember the specific plant used. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T2/T3 swap plague order (locusts before hail — real invert-trap); at T4 swap hyssop for palm branch / olive branch / vine (all real biblical plants); at T5 swap 'unleavened bread and bitter herbs' for 'wine and honey'. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T4 stem — 'They killed a lamb at twilight and brushed its blood on the doorposts with a bunch of what plant?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Apollo's plague on the Greek camp in Iliad Book 1 — a god's arrows falling on a people, then relenting. Named specifics carry the moral weight; no gloating over Egyptian suffering, no minimizing it either.
history_overlap: HISTORY owns Egyptian dynasty questions; theology owns the plague sequence.

name: The parting of the Red Sea
scope: T1: the Hebrews leave Egypt six hundred thousand men on foot besides children (Exodus 12:37), following a PILLAR OF CLOUD by day and a PILLAR OF FIRE by night (Exodus 13:21); they carry the bones of JOSEPH with them, as he made them swear. T2: Pharaoh's heart is hardened; he takes six hundred chosen CHARIOTS and pursues them, overtaking them encamped by the sea, PI-HAHIROTH before BAAL-ZEPHON; the people cry to Moses, 'Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness?' (Exodus 14:11). T3: Moses says, 'Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord' (Exodus 14:13); the angel of God and the pillar of cloud move behind them, standing between the two camps — darkness to the Egyptians, light to the Hebrews, all night. T4: Moses stretches out his HAND with his ROD over the sea; a strong EAST WIND blows all that night, and the waters are divided; the children of Israel go into the midst of the sea upon dry ground, the waters a WALL on their right hand and on their left (Exodus 14:22). T5: the Egyptians pursue after them into the sea; God takes off their chariot wheels so that they drive heavily; Moses stretches out his hand and the sea returns in the morning to its strength, and covers them; not one of them remains. On the far shore MIRIAM the prophetess, sister of Aaron, takes a TIMBREL in her hand and all the women follow her with timbrels and dancing, and she sings 'Sing ye to the Lord, for he hath triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea' (Exodus 15:20-21). Further rungs: the bitter waters of Marah made sweet by a tree cast in; the MANNA that falls white like coriander seed and tastes like wafers made with honey; the QUAILS that cover the camp; Moses striking the rock at Horeb and water gushing out (Exodus 17:6).
source: Grokipedia 'The Exodus' + 'Crossing the Red Sea' (browser); Exodus 12-15 KJV; primary: Exodus 13:21, 14:11-13, 14:22, 15:20-21.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T5 — MIRIAM'S TIMBREL SONG on the far shore. Most remember the parting, few remember the sister who leads the dance after. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T4 swap the wind direction (west / north / south — east is correct); at T5 swap Miriam's instrument for a lyre / a harp / a lute; at T4 swap 'wall on right and left' for 'stone bridge' / 'pillar of fire path'. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T4 stem — 'Moses stretched his rod over the sea. What kind of wind did God send that night?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the same awe as Odysseus's ships crushed between Scylla and Charybdis surviving by a hair — a passage through impossible water, marked and remembered.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY: 'Red Sea' vs 'Sea of Reeds' is a real translation debate — theology keeps 'Red Sea' as story-name.

name: Sinai, the tablets, and the golden calf
scope: T1: three months out of Egypt the Hebrews camp before MOUNT SINAI; on the third morning there are THUNDERS and LIGHTNINGS and a THICK CLOUD upon the mount, and the voice of a TRUMPET exceeding loud (Exodus 19:16); the whole mountain quakes greatly. T2: Moses goes up alone into the cloud and God speaks the TEN COMMANDMENTS — 'Thou shalt have no other gods before me ... Remember the sabbath day ... Honour thy father and thy mother ... Thou shalt not kill' (Exodus 20). T3: Moses stays on the mount FORTY DAYS AND FORTY NIGHTS, neither eating bread nor drinking water (Exodus 34:28); God gives him two TABLES OF STONE, written with the FINGER OF GOD (Exodus 31:18). T4: below, the people gather to AARON and say, 'Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses ... we wot not what is become of him' (Exodus 32:1); Aaron takes their GOLDEN EARRINGS, fashions a molten CALF, builds an altar, and proclaims a feast; the people rise up to play. T5: Moses comes down with the tablets in his hand and sees the calf and the dancing; his anger waxes hot and he casts the tables out of his hands and BREAKS THEM at the foot of the mount (Exodus 32:19); he burns the calf, grinds it to powder, strows it upon the water, and makes the children of Israel DRINK it. Further rungs: Moses's face SHINING when he comes down the second time so that he wears a VEIL (Exodus 34:29-35); the tablets written a second time; the ARK OF THE COVENANT built by BEZALEEL with two CHERUBIM of gold on the mercy seat; the pillar of cloud settling on the tabernacle.
source: Grokipedia 'Ten Commandments' + 'Golden calf' (browser); Exodus 19, 20, 31, 32, 34 KJV; primary: Exodus 19:16, 31:18, 32:1, 32:19, 34:29-35.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T5 — Moses making them DRINK the powdered gold calf in water. That detail is in the text and almost nobody remembers it. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T3 swap 'forty days' for 'seven days' / 'thirty days'; at T4 swap the calf material (bronze / silver / iron); at T5 swap 'broke them at the foot of the mount' for 'buried them' / 'threw them into the sea'. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T5 stem — 'Moses saw the calf and the dancing; he flung the two tablets from his hands and did what to them?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: the golden calf as told the same way you'd tell the Danes of Beowulf turning back to heathen sacrifices when Grendel came — a people's panic reaching for the old comforts. No 'idolatrous' scolding voice, just the story.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns Mount Sinai as a place-debate (Jebel Musa vs. others); theology owns the Sinai theophany.

name: Aaron's rod and the bronze serpent Nehushtan
scope: T1: after the golden calf, the twelve tribes murmur again against Aaron and his priesthood; Moses gathers twelve RODS, one for each tribe, and lays them up in the TABERNACLE before the testimony (Numbers 17:2-4). T2: in the morning AARON'S ROD, of the house of Levi, is BUDDED and has brought forth BUDS, and BLOOMED BLOSSOMS, and yielded ALMONDS (Numbers 17:8) — a dead stick alive overnight. T3: Moses brings out all the rods and every man takes his own; Aaron's rod is brought back and kept before the testimony as a token against the rebels; the rod is later remembered as one of the three things kept in the ark, with the pot of MANNA and the two tables of stone. T4: further along the wilderness journey the people speak against God and against Moses — 'wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness?' — and God sends FIERY SERPENTS among them, and many die (Numbers 21:5-6). T5: the people repent; God tells Moses, 'Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole'; Moses makes a serpent of BRASS and puts it on a pole, and it comes to pass that if a serpent has bitten any man, when he beholds the serpent of brass, he lives (Numbers 21:8-9); centuries later king HEZEKIAH breaks it in pieces, calling it NEHUSHTAN — 'a piece of brass' — because Israel had begun to burn incense to it (2 Kings 18:4). Further rungs: the pot of manna kept as a memorial; Korah, Dathan, and Abiram being swallowed by the earth just before the rod story; the bronze serpent as a WESTERN icon — the medical caduceus's rival ancestor.
source: Grokipedia 'Aaron's rod' + 'Nehushtan' (browser); Numbers 17, 21 KJV; 2 Kings 18 KJV; primary: Numbers 17:8, 21:8-9, 2 Kings 18:4.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T5 — HEZEKIAH later BREAKS the bronze serpent because people started worshipping the healing-relic itself. The reversal after centuries stuns. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T2 swap the fruit (figs / grapes / pomegranates — almonds is right); at T5 swap the destroyer-king (Josiah / Manasseh / David — Hezekiah is right; Josiah is the more famous reformer, so it's the mine); swap the name Nehushtan for other real object-names. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T2 stem — 'By morning Aaron's rod had budded, bloomed, and yielded what fruit?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Odin's staff Gungnir or Fionn's hazel-branch — a named object with its own history of veneration and rejection. No 'a type of Christ' Christian-typology reading forced in; the story stands on its own.
history_overlap: HISTORY owns Hezekiah as king of Judah c. 715-686 BCE; theology owns the Nehushtan story.

name: Joshua at Jericho: the trumpets and the walls
scope: T1: after Moses dies on Mount Nebo looking into the promised land, JOSHUA son of NUN leads Israel across the JORDAN — the priests bearing the ARK step into the river and the waters are cut off, rising up in a heap far from the city ADAM (Joshua 3:15-16); the people cross on dry ground. T2: Joshua sends two spies into JERICHO who lodge with RAHAB the harlot; she hides them under stalks of FLAX on her roof and lowers them out her window with a SCARLET CORD, which she must tie in the window to be spared when the city falls (Joshua 2:15, 2:18). T3: near Jericho Joshua sees a MAN with a drawn SWORD standing over against him; Joshua asks 'Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?' The man answers, 'Nay; but as CAPTAIN OF THE HOST OF THE LORD am I now come'; Joshua falls on his face (Joshua 5:13-14). T4: the seven priests bear seven TRUMPETS OF RAMS' HORNS before the ark; for six days the armed men and the ark compass the city ONCE around, and return to camp in silence. T5: on the SEVENTH DAY they rise early and compass the city SEVEN TIMES; at the seventh time the priests blow the trumpets and Joshua says, 'Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city' (Joshua 6:16); the people shout with a great shout and the WALL FALLS DOWN FLAT (Joshua 6:20), and they take the city, sparing only Rahab and her father's house at the sign of the scarlet cord. Further rungs: Achan's coveted BABYLONIAN GARMENT and wedge of gold hidden under his tent, and the defeat at Ai that follows; the second Ai attack with the ambush behind the city; Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal; the Gibeonites in worn shoes and mouldy bread getting a treaty by trickery.
source: Grokipedia 'Battle of Jericho' + 'Rahab' + 'Joshua' (browser); Joshua 2-6 KJV; primary: Joshua 2:15-18, 3:15-16, 5:13-14, 6:16-20.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T2 — RAHAB'S SCARLET CORD. The window-cord as the sparing-mark is proto-Passover and gets forgotten. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T4 swap 'rams' horns' for 'silver trumpets' (real, Numbers 10) / 'shofars of ivory'; at T5 swap seven times for three / twelve; at T2 swap 'scarlet cord' for 'blue cord' / 'purple thread' (both are real cultic colors). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T2 stem — 'Rahab tied something in her window as the sign that would spare her house. What color?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell the fall of Troy — a siege, a hidden agent inside the city (Sinon / Rahab), a signaled entry. No 'the true God gave them the land' framing; God as agent in the story, no more.
history_overlap: HISTORY: the archaeology of Jericho (Kathleen Kenyon) is contested; theology owns the story of the shout and the walls.

name: The defeat at Ai and Joshua's long day
scope: T1: after Jericho, Joshua sends three thousand men against AI, a small city, and they are ROUTED; thirty-six men die and 'the hearts of the people melted, and became as water' (Joshua 7:5). T2: Joshua tears his clothes and falls on his face before the ark; God tells him ISRAEL HAS SINNED and someone has taken of the accursed thing. Joshua brings the tribes near, then the families, then the households, then man by man — and the lot falls on ACHAN son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah (Joshua 7:16-18). T3: Achan confesses: 'I saw among the spoils a goodly BABYLONISH GARMENT, and two hundred shekels of SILVER, and a WEDGE OF GOLD of fifty shekels weight ... and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent' (Joshua 7:21); they take them out and stone Achan and his family in the valley of ACHOR. T4: Joshua returns against Ai with a hidden AMBUSH of thirty thousand behind the city; he draws out its army by feigned flight, then stretches out his SPEAR toward the city, and the ambush rises and takes it (Joshua 8:18-19). T5: later, defending the Gibeonites against five Amorite kings, Joshua asks the impossible — 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of AJALON' (Joshua 10:12) — and the SUN STANDS STILL and the moon stays until the people have avenged themselves upon their enemies, 'about a whole day' (Joshua 10:13). Further rungs: the great HAILSTONES that kill more of the fleeing enemy than the sword; the five kings hiding in the cave of MAKKEDAH and Joshua rolling a great stone against its mouth; the Book of JASHER cited as the source for the sun-standing verse.
source: Grokipedia 'Battle of Ai' + 'Joshua's Long Day' (browser); Joshua 7-8, 10 KJV; primary: Joshua 7:5, 7:21, 8:18-19, 10:12-13.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T5 — 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of AJALON' — the moon at Ajalon is the forgotten half. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T3 swap 'Babylonish garment' for a Persian robe / an Egyptian mantle (real spoils-types); at T5 swap Ajalon for Aijalon / Elah / Sorek (all real valleys); at T4 swap 'spear' for 'sword' / 'staff'. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T3 stem — 'Achan confessed he had hidden three things under his tent: a goodly what, silver, and a wedge of gold?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Roland's rearguard falling because Ganelon betrayed them at Roncesvalles — a battle-story of the one bad seed. Achan's family stoned is left in — no softening; Norse and Celtic myths don't get their cruelties softened either.
history_overlap: HISTORY: the archaeology of Ai (et-Tell vs. Khirbet el-Maqatir) is contested; theology owns the story-beats.

name: Samson: the honey in the lion, the jawbone, and the pillars
scope: T1: SAMSON is born to a barren woman of ZORAH visited by an angel, who tells her the boy shall be a NAZARITE from the womb — no wine, no unclean thing, and no RAZOR shall come upon his head (Judges 13:5); his strength lies in his hair. T2: going down to Timnath to see a Philistine woman he wants to marry, a young LION roars against him; Samson rends it as one would rend a kid, with nothing in his hand; later he returns and finds a swarm of BEES and HONEY in the lion's carcass, and he eats of it and gives to his parents without telling them where it came from (Judges 14:5-9). T3: at the wedding feast Samson tells a RIDDLE: 'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness' (Judges 14:14); his bride weeps until he tells her, she tells the Philistines, and Samson pays the thirty change of garments by slaying thirty men of Ashkelon. T4: bound with new ropes and given up to the Philistines by his own people, the ropes become as flax burnt with fire on his arms; he finds a JAWBONE of an ASS, new, and slays a thousand men with it — 'with the jawbone of an ass, heaps upon heaps, with the jaw of an ass have I slain a thousand men' (Judges 15:16); he calls the place RAMATH-LEHI ('the lifting up of the jawbone'). T5: DELILAH of the valley of SOREK is paid ELEVEN HUNDRED PIECES OF SILVER by each of the Philistine lords to learn the secret; three times he lies to her (seven green withs / new ropes / weaving his hair into the web of a loom), and at last he tells her true: 'there hath not come a razor upon mine head ... if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me' (Judges 16:17); she makes him sleep upon her knees and calls a man to shave off the seven locks of his head. Blinded and set to grind in Gaza, his hair grows again; at the temple feast to DAGON he asks the lad to place his hands on the two middle PILLARS of the house; he bows himself with all his might, saying 'Let me die with the Philistines' (Judges 16:30), and the house falls upon the lords and all the people. Further rungs: the foxes with firebrands in their tails burning the Philistine standing corn; Samson's death killing more than in his life; his burial between Zorah and Eshtaol in the buryingplace of Manoah his father.
source: Grokipedia 'Samson' + 'Delilah' (browser); Judges 13-16 KJV; primary: Judges 13:5, 14:5-14, 15:16, 16:17-30.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T3 — the RIDDLE 'out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness' being the lion-and-honey. Everyone knows Samson's strength, few remember the riddle text. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T4 swap jawbone-of-an-ass for jawbone-of-an-ox / jawbone-of-a-lion (parody-close); at T5 swap Delilah's bribe for real other biblical bribes (Judas 30, Joseph's 20); swap the god of the temple (Dagon is right; Baal / Chemosh / Moloch are traps). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T4 stem — 'Samson picked up a jawbone that lay on the ground — from what animal — and slew a thousand men?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Cuchulainn's ristrad and single combat at the ford — a berserker-hero with a specific vulnerability, betrayed by a woman close to him, dying in the collapse of the enemy hall. The parallel is real; the story stands on its own. Delilah's naming: no misogyny frame; she is a paid agent doing her work.
history_overlap: None direct.

name: Deborah, Barak, Sisera, and Jael's tent-peg
scope: T1: DEBORAH the prophetess, wife of Lapidoth, judges Israel under the PALM TREE of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim (Judges 4:5); she sends and calls BARAK son of Abinoam and tells him to take ten thousand men to Mount TABOR. T2: Barak answers, 'If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go' (Judges 4:8); Deborah says she will go — but 'the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the Lord shall sell SISERA into the hand of a WOMAN' (Judges 4:9). T3: SISERA, captain of Jabin king of Hazor, comes out with NINE HUNDRED CHARIOTS OF IRON to the river KISHON; the rain falls, the Kishon floods, the chariots bog in mud; Barak's men rout the host and Sisera flees away on his feet. T4: Sisera runs to the tent of JAEL wife of HEBER the Kenite; she welcomes him in, opens a bottle of MILK for him instead of the water he asks (Judges 5:25), covers him with a MANTLE, and stands at the door of the tent. T5: he sleeps; Jael takes a NAIL of the TENT (tent-peg) and a HAMMER in her hand, and 'she smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground' (Judges 4:21). Deborah sings her song — 'Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song' (Judges 5:12) — and pictures Sisera's mother waiting at the window: 'Why is his chariot so long in coming? why tarry the wheels of his chariots?' (Judges 5:28). Further rungs: the song of Deborah as one of the oldest passages in the Hebrew Bible; the tribes named for going and shamed for staying (Reuben abiding among the sheepfolds); 'the stars in their courses fought against Sisera' (Judges 5:20).
source: Grokipedia 'Deborah' + 'Jael' + 'Sisera' (browser); Judges 4-5 KJV; primary: Judges 4:8-9, 4:21, 5:12, 5:25, 5:28.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T4 — JAEL gives him MILK instead of water (in the song, 'butter in a lordly dish'). That hospitality-turned-trap detail is astonishing. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T5 swap the tent-peg for a sword / a knife / a millstone (the millstone is Abimelech's death in Judges 9 — real, adjacent); at T3 swap the river Kishon for the Kidron / Kishon / Arnon; at T2 swap Deborah's tree (palm) for oak / terebinth. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T5 stem — 'Sisera slept from exhaustion; Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through what?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the same cold precision you'd give the Morrigan or Judith of Bethulia — a woman warrior in an intimate-space kill. The song of Deborah's poetic quotes carry.
history_overlap: HISTORY owns Late Bronze / Iron I Canaan and the archaeology of chariot warfare; theology owns the tent-peg story.

name: Gideon: the fleece, the three hundred, and the trumpets in the jars
scope: T1: an angel finds GIDEON son of Joash threshing wheat by the WINEPRESS at OPHRAH to hide it from the MIDIANITES, whose camel raids have driven Israel into caves; the angel greets him, 'The Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour' (Judges 6:12). T2: Gideon asks for a sign; he lays a FLEECE of wool on the threshingfloor and asks that only the fleece be wet with DEW and the ground about it be dry — and in the morning he wrings a bowlful of water out of the fleece. Then he asks the reverse: 'let it now be DRY only upon the fleece, and upon all the ground let there be dew' (Judges 6:39-40); and so it is. T3: he gathers thirty-two thousand men; God says they are TOO MANY, lest Israel boast; he sends home the fearful (twenty-two thousand leave) and then brings the remaining ten thousand down to the WATER — those who bow down to drink kneeling are sent away, and only those who LAP with their tongues, putting HAND TO MOUTH like dogs, remain: THREE HUNDRED men (Judges 7:5-7). T4: at midnight Gideon divides the three hundred into three companies; he puts a TRUMPET into every man's hand, with empty PITCHERS, and LAMPS within the pitchers. At his sign they blow the trumpets and BREAK THE PITCHERS, holding the lamps in their left hands and the trumpets in their right, and cry 'The SWORD OF THE LORD, and of GIDEON' (Judges 7:20). T5: the Midianite host wakes in confusion and turns its swords upon itself; the enemy flees to the Jordan; Gideon captures the two Midianite princes ZEEB and OREB at the winepress and the rock and slays them; he refuses to be king — 'I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the Lord shall rule over you' (Judges 8:23) — but he takes their golden earrings and makes an EPHOD of the gold, which becomes a snare to his house. Further rungs: Gideon's midnight raid on his father's altar of Baal and the grove; the name JERUBBAAL ('let Baal contend') given him for tearing it down; the men of Succoth and Penuel refusing bread and being punished with thorns and briars; the death of Zebah and Zalmunna.
source: Grokipedia 'Gideon' + 'Gideon's Trumpets' (browser); Judges 6-8 KJV; primary: Judges 6:12, 6:39-40, 7:5-20, 8:23.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T3 — the LAPPING TEST at the water. Everyone knows 'three hundred', few remember the SELECTION method that produced them. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T2 swap the fleece for wool cast on stones / a garment left out (there is no other fleece-sign in scripture — this is uniquely Gideon's); at T4 swap the tools (torches / horns / drums are wrong; trumpets, pitchers, lamps are right); at T5 swap Oreb & Zeeb for Zebah & Zalmunna (both real, both Gideon's captives — a genuine mine). ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T3 stem — 'By the water God cut Gideon's ten thousand down to three hundred by watching how each man did what?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Leonidas at Thermopylae — a chosen few by a specific test, night assault, sound-and-terror routing a larger host. The parallel is honest, not overdrawn.
history_overlap: HISTORY owns the Iron Age camel-raid economy of Midian; theology owns the fleece and the three hundred.

name: Ruth gleaning in the field of Boaz
scope: T1: in the days of the judges a famine drives ELIMELECH of BETHLEHEM to MOAB with his wife NAOMI and their two sons Mahlon and Chilion; the sons marry Moabite women, ORPAH and RUTH; then all three men die, leaving three widows. T2: Naomi hears the famine is over and turns homeward; she tells her daughters-in-law to return to their mothers' houses; Orpah kisses her and goes back; but Ruth clings to her and says, 'Whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God' (Ruth 1:16). T3: they come to Bethlehem at the beginning of BARLEY HARVEST; the women say, 'Is this Naomi?' and Naomi answers, 'Call me not Naomi ('pleasant'), call me MARA ('bitter'): for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me' (Ruth 1:20). Ruth goes to GLEAN in the fields — the corners left standing for the poor by the law — and 'her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto BOAZ' (Ruth 2:3), a kinsman of Elimelech. T4: Boaz greets his reapers, 'The Lord be with you'; they answer, 'The Lord bless thee'; he sees Ruth and asks the reapers about her, then tells her to glean only in his fields, drink from his vessels, and take from the parched corn at meal; he charges his young men not to touch her, and lets HANDFULS FALL ON PURPOSE for her (Ruth 2:16). T5: at Naomi's counsel Ruth washes and anoints herself, goes down to the THRESHINGFLOOR at night, uncovers Boaz's feet as he sleeps by his heap of corn, and lies down; he wakes at midnight, startled, and she asks him to spread his skirt over her, for he is a NEAR KINSMAN. Boaz sends her home at dawn with SIX MEASURES of barley in her VEIL (Ruth 3:15); at the city gate he removes the SANDAL of the nearer kinsman who declines to redeem, and buys Elimelech's field and takes Ruth as wife (Ruth 4:7-10); their son OBED is born, father of Jesse, father of DAVID. Further rungs: the elders at the gate blessing Ruth with 'as Rachel and as Leah, which two did build the house of Israel'; the naming of Obed by the neighbor women; the genealogy that ends the book — Boaz, Obed, Jesse, David.
source: Grokipedia 'Book of Ruth' + 'Ruth (biblical figure)' (browser); Ruth 1-4 KJV; primary: Ruth 1:16, 1:20, 2:3-16, 3:15, 4:7-10.
framing_note: DINNER TEST: T5 — the SANDAL exchange at the gate is the ancient legal detail nobody remembers; and the SIX MEASURES OF BARLEY carried home in her veil at dawn. DISTRACTOR MINE: at T2 swap the quote-recipient (many misremember 'whither thou goest' as being to a husband); at T3 swap the harvest (wheat / barley / grape — barley is right, and it matters, since it precedes wheat harvest); at T5 swap the removed-shoe custom for other real Levirate rituals. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: T2 stem — 'One daughter-in-law kissed Naomi and went back to Moab; the other clung to her and said what?' SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told the way you'd tell Andromache staying with Hector's people, or the loyalty pledges in Njal's Saga — a foreigner-widow choosing kinship in exile. No forced 'ancestor-of-Jesus' Christian typology; the David-ancestor line at the end is a plain story-beat that this ladder can name honestly, without theological gloss.
history_overlap: None direct; the David-ancestry is genealogy in the story itself.
